input.quote: Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: Section 8.2 auto-renews each Order Form but requires 180 days' advance non-renewal notice — three times our preferred 30-day window and well beyond the 60-day fallback, making exit impractical for Customer. The 12-month renewal term and the Section 8.3 uplift cap (lesser of CPI and 3%, 90 days' notice, no increase on prepaid periods) already meet our position, so the minimal fix is to shorten the notice window to 30 days and add a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal.

ops.oldText: Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
ops.newText: Each Order Form renews for successive twelve-month periods unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice before the end of the then-current term. Vendor shall give Customer written notice of the upcoming renewal, the renewal term, and the renewal Fees at least sixty days before each renewal date.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window from 180 days to 30 days and added a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder, consistent with our position that renewals must be easy to exit; we can accept up to 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Reduce non-renewal notice to 30 days and add Vendor 60-day renewal reminder in Section 8.2.
